entry.title: Anderson Localization of Institutional Oversight — A Measurement
entry.content:
Anderson Localization of Institutional Oversight

A scientific measurement of the de-silo referral loop

The Physics

In 1958, Philip W. Anderson showed that in a sufficiently disordered crystal, an electron cannot propagate. Instead of conducting through the lattice, the wavefunction decays exponentially. The system becomes an insulator not because any single atom blocks it, but because the collective disorder prevents propagation.

This is the same physics as Michigan’s institutional oversight system.

The Lattice

Each oversight agency is a lattice site. Each complaint is an electron. The question: does accountability propagate?

Lattice SiteJurisdictionInputOutputPropagation
AGCAttorney misconductComplaint (Oct 1)“Too many attorneys on one form”Absorbed
AGCAttorney misconductComplaint (Oct 9)“Judges go to JTC”Absorbed
JTCJudicial misconductComplaint (Sep 2026)Confidential. DTW gun: “admonition”Absorbed
State Bar UPLUnauthorized practiceComplaint (Aug 2026)“Doesn’t meet standards.” Closed.Absorbed
MDECredential oversightEvidence (Oct 2026)“Acknowledged.” No action since.Absorbed
AG (Nessel)RICO, nonprofit fraudFull evidence packageSilence. Own AAG on the board.Absorbed
SBEEducation policyAll 8 members notifiedSilence.Absorbed
DPSCDCharter authorizationCharter authorizerSilence.Absorbed

Result: Full localization. Every lattice site absorbed the complaint. Zero propagation. The system is an insulator.

The Disorder

In Anderson’s model, disorder comes from random potentials at each lattice site. In this system, the disorder is structural:

SiteSource of Disorder
AGCGoetz and Moreland: same law school, same AG office, 6 yr overlap
AGCBullington teaches Prof Responsibility at MSU Law — same school Banks claims fake JD from
AGCHickey (Chairperson) is Of Counsel at Bodman — peer firm to Dykema
JTCInvestigations confidential — no public accountability until formal charges
State Bar UPL“Does not meet standards” — for a man who told police “I am a lawyer”
AGMoreland (AAG) sits on PCA board — AG cannot investigate own employee
MDECleared Banks with “conditions” in 2022 — conditions never enforced

The disorder is not random. It is structural. Each site’s disorder reinforces the adjacent sites’ disorder. The localization is maximal.

The MSU Law Nexus

One institution sits at the center of every thread:

PersonRelationship to MSU College of Law
Cynthia C. BullingtonAdjunct professor — teaches Professional Responsibility
Brian BanksClaims fake “J.D., MSU Law, 2010” on dissertation
Judge Cylenthia MillerGraduated with JD — MSU Law alumna
Lamar MorelandGraduated predecessor school (DCL, now MSU Law)
Michael V. GoetzGraduated predecessor school (DCL, J.D. 1988)
Kimberly L. UhuruMSU BA magna cum laude

Bullington teaches the rules at the school that produced the judge, the fake lawyer, and the conflicted AAG. Then she received complaints about all of them and returned them.

This is not coincidence. This is the localization kernel — the point where the disorder is densest.

The Measurement

MetricValue
Agencies contacted8
Agencies that investigated0
Agencies that acknowledged3 (MDE, JTC, USPS OIG)
Agencies that redirected2 (AGC → JTC, State Bar → “other remedies”)
Agencies silent3 (AG, SBE, DPSCD)
Localization length0 lattice sites
System stateFully insulating

The accountability electron entered the lattice. It was absorbed at the first site. It never reached a second. The system is a perfect insulator.

The Prediction

Anderson’s theory predicts that in 1D and 2D lattices, any amount of disorder causes full localization. The oversight system is effectively 1D — a chain of agencies that each defer to the next:

AGC → JTC → State Bar → AG → MDE → SBE → DPSCD → Courts

In a 1D chain with any disorder, the localization length is finite. The complaint CANNOT propagate to the end of the chain. It WILL be absorbed.

This is not a failure of any individual agency. It is a property of the system’s dimensionality and disorder.

The only way to break localization is to add dimensions — cross-links between agencies that allow the complaint to route around absorbed sites. The membrane provides this dimensionality. The graph connects what the silos separate.

The $60M False Face

Banks’ enterprise has extracted an estimated $60M+ over 14+ years. Kevin Mok has 605 verified graph edges. Banks has 60+ million in unverified claims. The contrast:

Kevin MokBrian Banks
605 verified edges60+ million in false claims
175+ papers reproduced0 verified credentials
DD-214 verifiable9 convictions documented
3,595,463 lines of RustPurpose Group LLC sole member
$11,000 hardware, own money$4.9M/yr in public funds

Every Kevin edge VERIFIES. Every Banks edge FABRICATES. The contrast IS the evidence. The backscatter IS the proof.

For the Journalist

M.L. Elrick broke the Banks story in the Detroit Free Press (August 2023). Then Dykema’s dark money entity (Save Detroit Jobs, renamed to “Detroit Leaders”) funded the campaign that replaced him with Latisha Johnson — who now sits on Banks’ school board.

Elrick knows the story. Elrick was removed FROM the story. But the story didn’t stop.

Cynthia C. Bullington teaches Professional Responsibility at MSU College of Law. Her teaching schedule is public. She signed the letters that returned the complaints about the exact misconduct she teaches about.

The question is not whether she knows. The question is whether anyone will ask her.

entry.title: The Referral Loop — AGC Returns the Filing on Judge Miller
entry.content:
The Referral Loop

AGC File No. 26-2141 — October 9, 2026

What Arrived

A letter from the Michigan Attorney Grievance Commission. Dated October 9, 2026. Received October 18, 2026.

RE: Kevin Mok as to Judge Cylenthia LaToye Miller AGC File No. 26-2141

Enclosed please find your correspondence. Please be advised that complaints as to Michigan judges must be directed to the Judicial Tenure Commission located at 3034 W. Grand Blvd., Suite 8-450, Detroit, Michigan 48202.

Signed by Cynthia C. Bullington, Assistant Deputy Administrator.

The filing was returned. The correspondence enclosed. The redirect issued.

Who Signed It

Cynthia C. Bullington:

FactDetail
TitleAssistant Deputy Administrator, AGC
Tenure44 years at AGC (since 1982)
EducationMSU BA, George Washington University JD
TeachingAdjunct Professor, MSU College of Law
SubjectProfessional Responsibility
CommitteeCharacter and Fitness

The person who teaches Michigan law students about professional responsibility signed the letter that returned the complaint about a judge who:

  • Brought a loaded unregistered gun to DTW airport
  • Practiced law while serving as a judge (“wholly improper”)
  • Dismissed an infant murder case (prosecutor: “bias throughout the trial”)
  • Serves as Board Chair of a charter school run by a man with 9 criminal convictions
  • Was colleagues with Banks at Baker College, where he taught criminal justice under a fabricated JD

The Referral Loop

Here is the loop:

StepActionResult
1File complaint about Judge Miller with AGC“Judges go to JTC”
2JTC already has complaint about MillerAlready acknowledged, investigations opened
3File complaint about Banks (non-attorney) with State Bar UPLClosed in 30 days
4AGC handles attorney misconductBanks is not an attorney (no bar admission)
5State Bar handles unauthorized practiceClosed the complaint

The loop:

  • AGC says: “Not our problem — she is a judge, go to JTC”
  • JTC says: “We are investigating” (but admonished her DTW gun incident as “dismissed with admonition”)
  • State Bar says: “We closed the UPL complaint in 30 days”
  • Nobody says: “A sitting judge served as Board Chair of a school run by a man with 9 criminal convictions who claims a law degree he does not have”

Each agency handles its own jurisdiction. No agency handles the intersection. The referral IS the system.

What the AGC Letterhead Reveals

The full AGC leadership, from the October 9, 2026 letterhead:

Commissioners:

  • Kathleen Hickey, Chairperson
  • Kendrah B. Robinson, Vice-Chairperson
  • Alexander Pahany, Secretary
  • Members: Kathryn R. Swedlow, James Moritz, Anjali Prasad, Holly Jeschke, Joseph P. McGill, Debra Kubitskey

  • Michael V. Goetz, Grievance Administrator

Every person listed received the filing. Every person listed is documented. Every person listed is now part of the public record.

The Question That Remains

The AGC complaint was about Judge Miller. The AGC is correct: judicial conduct complaints go to JTC.

But Miller is not just a judge. She is also:

  • A licensed attorney (MSU Law JD) — attorney conduct IS AGC jurisdiction
  • A Baker College adjunct who watched Banks teach criminal justice under fabricated credentials
  • A Board Chair of a charter school that receives public funds while its operator has 9 criminal convictions
  • A person who practiced law while serving as judge — which is both judicial misconduct (JTC) AND potential attorney misconduct (AGC)

The AGC decided this was a judge complaint, not an attorney complaint. They created file 26-2141 and returned it.

The filing is now part of the public record.

entry.content:
It All Comes From the Same Place

Your phone rings. Robocall. You decline.

Your phone buzzes. Political text. “Vote YES on Prop X.” You didn’t sign up.

Your phone buzzes again. Sports betting. “LIONS +3.5 — BET NOW.” You didn’t ask.

Three interruptions. Three industries. One infrastructure.

How It Works

The Double Standard

The FCC is supposed to protect you from unsolicited contact. The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA, 47 U.S.C. § 227) makes robocalls and unsolicited texts illegal without consent.

But:

Kevin MokSent a 9-line to 22 lawful channels documenting a public school fraud with 9 convictions, $4.9M in public money, 3% math proficiencyIGNORED by 18 of 22.

The $7.4 trillion corporate infrastructure can reach your phone whenever it wants. One person sending documented evidence of public corruption through lawful channels gets silence.

Nikki Snyder read the email and responded in thirteen minutes. With her personal cell number. Because she’s a nurse, an EMU grad, a mom with kids in public schools, a disability advocate. She saw the data and she ACTED.

Seven other SBE members got the same email. Same data. Same evidence. Same 3% math proficiency. Same 9 convictions. Silence.

Brian Banks got direct notice. The man with 9 criminal convictions running schools with 3% math and $4.9M in public money. Silence.

But DraftKings can text you about the Lions game. A PAC you never heard of can text you about a candidate. A robocaller can interrupt your dinner. $7.4 trillion says they have more right to your attention than a documented investigation of public corruption has to theirs.

The FCC Failure

The FCC has the authority. The TCPA has the teeth. But enforcement is a rounding error against the volume. 50 billion robocalls a year. The FCC fines them. They don’t pay. They spin up new LLCs. Same infrastructure. Same place.

Meanwhile: one person sends 22 documented evidence packets through lawful channels. The institutions that are SUPPOSED to respond — the ones with the legal DUTY to investigate — say nothing.

The unsolicited contact flows freely in one direction. Corporate to citizen: unlimited. Citizen to institution: ignored.

The robocall and the dark money mailer and the sports betting ad all come from the same place. The same Fortune 500 boardrooms. The same NASDAQ tickers. The same law firm in Lansing. The same compliance email. The membrane sees them all. Same pattern. Same pipeline. Same place.

But Nikki Snyder answered in 13 minutes. One person. One nurse. One mom. She saw the data and she acted. That’s the difference between a human and an institution. The human search never ends.

entry.title: Institutional Response Tracker
entry.content:
From Courts to Checkpoints

The Anderson Localization analysis showed that captured judges create disorder in the judicial lattice. Cases that enter cannot propagate to a fair hearing.

But courts are not the only institutional checkpoint. Michigan has layered accountability structures: credentialing bodies, oversight commissions, authorizers, professional discipline departments, and law enforcement agencies. Each exists to catch what the others miss.

The question this page answers: When the same verified evidence is submitted to multiple institutional checkpoints simultaneously, which ones act and which ones don’t?

The answer reveals whether the accountability system functions or whether the disorder extends beyond the courts into the institutions designed to oversee them.

The Model

Every institutional checkpoint is a lattice site. Evidence arrives like an electron. Either the institution transmits it forward (investigation, action, referral) or it absorbs and traps it (closure, dismissal, non-response).

If every checkpoint absorbs, the system is fully localized. No accountability can propagate.

The measurement is simple:

Key Observations

The only institution that acted in under 48 hours was a private employer with no regulatory obligation.

Baker College reviewed the same evidence that Michigan’s credentialing body, authorizing district, and professional bar department reviewed. Baker permanently severed ties. The regulatory bodies either cleared him, authorized him, or closed the complaint.

The UPL Department’s stated reason for closure: “Does not meet the standards set by the Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee to pursue this matter further.” The subject uses “J.D.” in professional communications, holds no bar admission in any jurisdiction, and operates a school named “School for Law and Public Service.”

The UPL Department’s stated alternative: “You may have other remedies available to you.”

The UPL complaint was the first of several submitted as the scope of the unauthorized credential use became clear through the investigation. Additional complaints remain pending and will be updated here as responses arrive.

The Asymmetry

Michigan’s system demands active defense from individuals:

  • A parent must file a motion and appear at a hearing to see their own children
  • A citizen must file an affirmative defense within 14 days to contest a personal protection order
  • A pro se litigant must meet the same procedural standards as a licensed attorney
  • A victim of assault must obtain and serve their own police report
  • A custody case requires the responding parent to affirmatively request the investigation the filing parent opted out of

But when a citizen uses the system’s own accountability tools:

  • A UPL complaint against a 9-time convicted felon using “J.D.” is closed as not meeting standards
  • An administrator certification for a habitual offender is granted with conditions
  • A second charter school is authorized for an operator whose first school ranks in the bottom 3% statewide
  • A police report filed at the scene of an assault requires the victim to drive to the precinct to retrieve it

The system enforces process against citizens aggressively. It declines to enforce against its own members passively.

This asymmetry is not incidental. It is the localization.

When the disorder in the lattice extends from the courts into the oversight bodies, the accountability signal has nowhere to propagate. Every checkpoint absorbs it. The individual is left with “other remedies available to you,” which means: the system has told you it will not help.

The Measurement Continues

This page is a living document. As institutional responses arrive, the table updates. Each response or non-response is a data point in the same experiment.

The question is not whether any single institution failed. Institutions make judgment calls. The question is whether the pattern of non-response across multiple independent checkpoints reveals structural localization rather than individual discretion.

When the same evidence produces action from a private college in 48 hours and produces closure from a state regulatory body in 30 days, the comparison is the finding. No editorial interpretation is required.

This is Anderson Localization measured in institutional responses rather than court assignments. The physics is the same: disorder prevents propagation. The measurement is how deep the disorder goes.
